items.title: Johor health exco warns of scam using his identity
items.summary: In a Facebook post, he said several acquaintances had contacted him after receiving a voice message this afternoon. "The individual also said he wanted to borrow money. "When asked to make a phone call, the individual contacted my friend, but his voice sounded suspicious," he said.

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against major currencies, easier vs greenback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended higher against a basket of major currencies but slid against the US dollar on Thursday, as the greenback remained well supported despite waning expectations of an interest rate hike by the United States (US) Federal Reserve (Fed). At 6pm, the ringgit fell to 4.0830/4.0875 against the US dollar from Wednesday's close of 4.0785/4.0820. "Despite that, the US dollar remains well supported with the US dollar Index rising by 0.30 per cent to 101.759 points," he told Bernama.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM OCT 1, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia closed lower today as cautious sentiment grew amid weaker domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign selling. The cautious mood kept the FBM KLCI under pressure, with local institutional buying providing some support as foreign funds continued to exit. That wraps up today's Market Pulse.

items.title: Bidor shooting: Police take statements from nine witnesses
items.summary: IPOH: Perak police have recorded statements from nine people, including the victim, in their investigation into the shooting of a businessman at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral last Tuesday. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said those whose statements were recorded included three family members who were in the victim's vehicle, two people in a vehicle near the scene and employees of the petrol station. He said the victim is now in stable condition after receiving treatment and undergoing surgery at Seri Botani Hospital, while police are investigating from various angles, including identifying the motive, which has yet to be established.

items.title: Sarawak sees improved air quality as unhealthy readings fall
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Four areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.30pm today, down from 10 areas recorded earlier in the day. Meanwhile, 57 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings. Selangor's Shah Alam recorded 98, followed by Banting (97), Petaling Jaya (91) and Kuala Selangor (76), while in Negri Sembilan, Port Dickson recorded 95 and Seremban 93.

items.title: 8 cops arrested in Taman Keramat ketum raid
items.summary: "A team of policemen from the Bukit Aman Integrity and Standards Compliance Department's Intelligence and Operations Branch, assisted by the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters' Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division, raided a premises in Jalan AU 1, Taman Keramat, at 8.45pm. "Eight lower-ranking police officers were arrested during the raid. "Seven of them are attached to various units under the Sentul district police headquarters, while another is attached to the Brickfields district police headquarters.

items.title: KKB Engineering lands RM517mil Sarawak water job
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KKB Engineering Bhd has bagged a RM517 million contract from the government through the Regional Corridor Development Authority (Recoda) for the Samalaju Phase 2 water supply infrastructure project in Sarawak. In a bourse filing, the engineering company said it accepted the contract under the Sarawak Corridor of Renewable Energy with a completion period of 36 months. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Anwar joins pit lane walk ahead of Sepang F1 return
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today joined a pit lane walk at the Sepang International Circuit ahead of the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, which returns to Malaysia this weekend. Anwar was seen walking through the busy pit lane as teams made final preparations for the race, with mechanics, equipment and activity around the garages offering a close-up look at preparations ahead of the race weekend. Yesterday, SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said the circuit is fully prepared ahead of the race, with nearly 100,000 tickets sold, setting a record for the highest ticket sales in the history of races held at the circuit.

items.title: IDEAS urges institutional reforms in 2027 Budget
items.summary: "Institutional reform cannot wait for another budget cycle. The government must prioritise enactment of institutional reforms," the Institute for Democracy and Economic Affairs (IDEAS) said in a statement. IDEAS said relevant agencies, including the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department, Attorney-General's Chambers, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission and Election Commission, should be adequately funded to advance institutional reforms.

items.title: Sunway Healthcare confident after GIC exit
items.summary: DAMANSARA: Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd is confident of continued investor support following the disposal of Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC's remaining five per cent stake in the healthcare group. Sunway Healthcare executive chairman Tan Sri Dr Jeffrey Cheah said the sale of about 575 million shares by GIC's investment vehicle, Greenwood Capital Pte Ltd, marked the final tranche of its holdings in the listed healthcare operator. Cheah said a significant portion of the shares had been taken up by local institutions, including Permodalan Nasional Bhd and the Employees Provident Fund, reflecting continued institutional interest in Sunway Healthcare.

items.title: Marine police arrest 2,707 in 7,627 maritime crime cases
items.summary: PORT KLANG: Marine police have arrested 2,707 people in 7,627 criminal cases in the country's waters during the first nine months of this year. "The highest number of offences involved the Fisheries Act, with 3,214 cases, followed by offences under the Dangerous Drugs Act, Control of Supplies Act (295), Immigration Act and Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act (213), as well as the Customs Act (189)," he said at a press conference after officiating the Marine Police 79th anniversary celebrations. Meanwhile, Yusri said the Marine Police had 22 projects under the Malaysia Plan, spanning the 11th to 13th Malaysia Plans, worth RM1.064 billion.

items.title: Don't abuse your power, deputy IGP tells police
items.summary: Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid said leadership was not a privilege to be used for personal gain but a major trust that must be discharged responsibly. “Therefore, I urge that every decision made must be based on integrity, accountability and a sense of fairness,” he said at the handover ceremony for the Sarawak acting police commissioner and acting chairman of the Sarawak Contingent Persatuan Keluarga Polis (Perkep) at the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters here today. Earlier, he witnessed the handover of duties from PDRM Management Department director Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah, who was also the Sarawak police commissioner, to his deputy DCP Saifullizan Ishak before Mohamad Zainal begins his duties at Bukit Aman.

items.title: Perkeso boosts benefits for more than 7mil contributors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than seven million Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributors stand to benefit from enhanced Employment Insurance System (EIS) benefits that take effect today. Perkeso said the improvements under amendments to the Employment Insurance System Act 2017 would provide an average benefit of about RM3,300 per person and help workers return to employment. The amendments also introduce a new RM1,000 mobility assistance allowance, paid as a one-off benefit to contributors who lose their jobs, receive EIS benefits and secure new employment more than 100km from their homes.

items.title: Johor to halt projects blamed for flash floods, mudflows
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Development projects in Johor found to have caused flash floods or mudflows in surrounding areas will be immediately shut down, said the state Housing and Local Government Committee. Its chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said action will be taken against developers and contractors who failed to comply with development approval conditions, particularly requirements for retention ponds and centralised drainage systems. Jafni said all housing and other development project developers in Johor Baru would be called for a briefing and stern reminder on flood mitigation requirements.

items.title: KKDW RM2.1 billion overspending issue resolved – Treasury deputy secretary-general
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The issue concerning claims that the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) had overspent RM2.1 billion against its allocations between 2023 and 2025 has been resolved, said Treasury deputy secretary-general (Policy) Datuk Zamzuri Abdul Aziz. The issue arose following claims that KKDW spent RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an allocation of RM1.1 billion, RM2 billion in 2024 against RM1.3 billion and RM2.3 billion in 2025 against RM1.6 billion, resulting in a total deficit of RM2.1 billion. On Sept 2, Johan explained that KKDW had made commitments and spent beyond its approved annual allocations for rural road projects.

items.title: Nepal move to verify status brings hope, relief to missing Malaysians' families
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of Malaysians still missing following last month's mudslide disaster in Nepal have welcomed the Nepali government's decision to expedite the process of verifying the victims' status. Hani Othman, wife of Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, better known as Loe, said she was relieved by the decision after waiting for more than a month for certainty over her husband's fate. She said she was still experiencing mixed emotions, holding on to hope that her husband would be found while recognising that the families also needed certainty over the status of those still missing.

items.title: Unemployed man jailed, fined RM3k for cheating e-hailing driver
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: An unemployed man was jailed for five days and fined RM3,000 by the magistrate's court here for cheating an e-hailing driver with a fake payment receipt. Magistrate A. Shaarmini imposed the sentence on B. Parameswara, 26, after he pleaded guilty to cheating Mohd Firdaus Md Naim by presenting the receipt. KW: unemployed man, e-hailing driver, fake payment receipt, cheating, magistrate's court, Johor Jaya, Penal Code, Nst, News, Malaysia © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysia’s marine police nab 2,707, record 7,627 cases in national waters this year
items.summary: Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said that the success was the result of continuous enforcement through various operations such as Op Taring Gelora, Op Taring Landai, and inter or intra-agency operations. “The highest offences among them involve the Fisheries Act 1985 with 3,214 cases, the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 (428), the Control of Supplies Control Act 1961 (295), the Immigration Act 1959/63 and the ATIPSOM Act 2007 (213), as well as the Customs Act 1967 (189 cases),” he said at a press conference after officiating the 79th Anniversary celebration of the PPM at the Region One PPM Operations headquarters, Pulau Indah here today. Meanwhile, Mohd Yusri said that PPM as a whole now has 22 projects under the Malaysia Plan (11MP to 13MP) worth RM1.064 billion.

items.title: Malaysia plans A-to-D food grades to nudge manufacturers — and consumers — towards healthier choices
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia could introduce a new food labelling system giving packaged food and drinks nutrition grades from A to D by the end of this year, Health Ministry official Dr Yap Wei Aun has said. Dr Yap, chief executive officer of the Health Ministry’s Health Transformation Office, said prevention was a fundamental aspect of public health and cited the proposed labelling system as an example of the government’s preventive health initiatives. Dr Yap said the Health Ministry had been working with partners, including the food industry, to introduce the “front-of-pack labelling” system, under which bottles of drinks or packaged food would carry an A, B, C or D grade.

items.title: Perodua Alza overturns after chain collision on Federal Highway
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Three vehicles were involved in a crash at Km14.1 of the Federal Highway heading from Klang towards Kuala Lumpur this morning. The accident, which occurred around 7.20am, involved a Perodua Myvi, a Perodua Alza and an Isuzu D-Max. The collision caused the Myvi to hit the D-Max in front, while the Alza skidded and overturned onto its left side.

items.title: Netizens rally behind Shuhaily after KLIA viral video
items.summary: Well done, Datuk Shuhaily." the user wrote. "Datuk Shuhaily is the best.

items.title: UK PM Burnham sows seeds of "Breturn" that could excite markets
items.summary: NEVER mind Britain's stretched budget numbers. Even a whiff of "Breturn" could move sterling assets. At his Labour Party's annual conference on Tuesday, Burnham, who campaigned to stay in the EU in a 2016 Brexit referendum, argued the nation should again consider options for "Britain's long-term relationship with our European partners."

items.title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning issued for KL, 10 states until 7pm
items.summary: In Kedah, the affected areas are Kuala Muda, Sik and Baling, while in Perak, they are Hulu Perak, Selama, Kerian, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk. In Kelantan, the warning covers Kuala Krai and Jeli. Similar warnings were issued for Terengganu, covering Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu; Pahang, covering Rompin, Maran, Temerloh and Bera; and Selangor, covering Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Gombak, Petaling, Sepang and Kuala Langat.

items.title: Three separate drug busts net RM3.44m in drugs, five arrests in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police arrested five people, including a couple, and seized various types of drugs worth RM3.44 million in three separate operations between September 21 and 27. Penang Police Chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the raids by the state Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) resulted in the seizure of 8.83 kilogrammes (kg) of heroin, 15.06 kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) powder, five litres of liquid MDMA, 182 ecstasy pills and 70 grammes (g) of ketamine. Lim said police seized 3.26 kg of MDMA powder and five litres of liquid MDMA, estimated to be worth RM1.2 million, while investigations found that the couple worked at entertainment centres and obtained the MDMA supply from a drug distribution syndicate.

items.title: F1 fever builds as PM Anwar takes pit-lane walk at Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Formula 1 fever moved up a gear at the Sepang International Circuit today as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim joined a Pit Lane Walk on the eve of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. This weekend’s race marks Formula 1’s return to Sepang after a nine-year absence, with the circuit last hosting a world championship round in 2017. Interest has been strong, with nearly 100,000 tickets sold as of Wednesday — a record for races held at the circuit, according to Sepang International Circuit chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif.

items.title: Afghan tourist's cause of death in Pulau Tioman pending lab analysis
items.summary: ROMPIN: The cause of death of an Afghan tourist who fell unconscious while diving off Pulau Tioman yesterday remains undetermined pending laboratory analysis of post-mortem findings. Rompin police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said the post-mortem, which began at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital in Kuantan around 10am today, had yet to determine the cause of death. "The medical team requires further laboratory assessments following several findings from the post-mortem examination.

items.title: Finance Ministry: Monthly SARA aid credited to recipients’ MyKad from today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid has begun being credited to recipients through their respective MyKad cards from today. The Finance Ministry (MoF), in a post on X today, said RM100 in monthly SARA aid would be credited to households receiving Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR), while senior citizens and single individuals would each receive RM50 a month. For recipients of both STR and eKasih, households will receive RM200 in monthly SARA aid, while senior citizens will receive RM150 and single individuals RM100.

items.title: Weather alert: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across KL, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Labuan and 10 states until 7pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather was expected to affect several areas in Kedah, namely Kuala Muda, Sik and Baling; Perak, including Hulu Perak, Selama, Kerian, Larut Matang, Kuala Kangsar, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk; and Kelantan, covering Kuala Krai and Jeli. The same warning was issued for Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; Rompin, Maran, Temerloh and Bera in Pahang; and Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Gombak, Petaling, Sepang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, reported Bernama.

items.title: 'Loud thud': Sperm whale sinks yacht in South Pacific
items.summary: WELLINGTON: A sperm whale cracked the hull of a yacht sailing in the remote South Pacific, forcing four sailors into a day-and-night fight for survival on the high seas. Crew members on the 16-metre Tai Tam told AFP on Thursday of their weekend encounter with a pod of sperm whales 250 nautical miles north of tiny Norfolk Island. The whole boat was pushed sideways," said Australian Jemma Cooper, who was thrown from the steering wheel by the force of the blow.

items.title: Health Ministry warns against GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after mercury found
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has cancelled the notification of the cosmetic product GB Daily Glow Skin Cream after it was found to contain scheduled poisons, mercury, and is no longer allowed to be sold in the country. Following that, the ministry urged the public to avoid buying and using the involved cosmetics. The statement said that the involved sellers and distributors of the cosmetics must immediately cease the sale and distribution of the cosmetics.

items.title: Johor allocates RM30mil to tackle flash floods in city
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Johor government will allocate an additional RM30 million to implement four immediate measures, covering short- and medium-term solutions, to address flash floods in the city. He was commenting on yesterday's flash floods that affected several areas, including Kampung Mohd Amin, Kampung Pasir and Jalan Ayer Molek. Mohd Jafni said several immediate measures would also begin tomorrow.

items.title: Anwar thanks outgoing Chinese ambassador for strengthening bilateral ties
items.summary: In a Facebook post, Anwar said Ouyang had demonstrated commitment and contributed towards strengthening cooperation between the two countries in various fields, including the economy, technology, education and culture. "Malaysia and China have built a strong bond in various fields, including economy, technology, education, and culture," he said. Anwar said strategic cooperation involving the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL), 5G technology, artificial intelligence (AI), ports and the rare earth industry had also opened new avenues for mutual benefit.

items.title: Iran Guards hail US withdrawal from Iraq as 'historic victory'
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's Revolutionary Guards on Thursday welcomed the withdrawal of US forces from Iraq as a "historic victory" and called for American troops to leave the Middle East. The Revolutionary Guards "congratulate the proud nation of Iraq, the united front of the Islamic Resistance, and the revolutionary fighters of the Islamic world on this historic victory," the guards said in a statement carried by their official media. On Wednesday the US-led coalition that deployed to Iraq and Syria in 2014 to fight the Islamic State (IS) group formally concluded its mission and withdrew.

items.title: Gravedigger jailed a month for stealing RM16 from surau donation box
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A gravedigger was jailed a month by the magistrate's court here today for stealing RM16 from a surau donation box at a shopping mall. Magistrate A. Shaarmini ordered Nazarudin Mahmud, 45, to serve the sentence from the date of his arrest. Nazarudin stole the cash from the surau donation box at Angsana Johor Baru Mall at 4.20pm on Monday.

items.title: Indonesia remains a favourite destination for Malaysians as August arrivals jump nearly 29pc
items.summary: JAKARTA, Oct 1 — Malaysians remained Indonesia’s largest source of foreign tourists in August, with arrivals jumping 28.95 per cent year-on-year to 296,227. According to Statistics Indonesia (BPS), Malaysian visitors accounted for 18.52 per cent of the 1.60 million foreign tourist arrivals recorded during the month. BPS said overall foreign tourist arrivals in August rose 6.27 per cent from a year earlier, while arrivals from January to August reached 10.58 million, up 5.38 per cent from the corresponding period in 2025.

items.title: Saravanan questions MACC over son's presence at headquarters
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan has criticised the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission's (MACC) explanation for his 12-year-old son's presence at its headquarters on Monday, describing it as "entirely illogical". MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said today that the commission did not serve an asset declaration notice on Saravanan's 12-year-old son. He said the boy's presence at the MACC headquarters was as a companion to his parents and not to receive an asset declaration notice.

items.title: 35 years, 12 strokes for man who robbed, raped and murdered woman
items.summary: Judicial Commissioner Steve Ritikos imposed the sentence on Md Ridzuan Abd Ahmad Zaini Logan, 37, after considering submissions by the prosecution and defence on the appropriate sentence. Deputy public prosecutor Nur Nisla Abd Latif had sought the death penalty or, alternatively, the maximum 40-year prison sentence. In her submission on aggravating factors, she said that although the Abolition of Mandatory Death Penalty Act 2023 had come into force, the death penalty could still be imposed in certain cases, citing several court decisions in which the death penalty had been imposed after the Act came into force.

items.title: Pupil who suffered broken leg after being slammed by ustaz wins appeal, awarded RM47,000
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A pupil who suffered a broken right leg after being slammed by an ustaz during a Kafa class has won his appeal at the High Court, more than four years after the incident. Lawyer Mohd Hazwan Hamidun said the High Court allowed his client's appeal against the Kuala Terengganu Sessions Court's decision to dismiss the claim. "The case was initially filed at the Sessions Court, but the court dismissed the plaintiff's claim.

items.title: Kuala Terengganu High Court awards RM47,000 to boy who broke leg after being ‘slammed’ onto chair by teacher
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — The Kuala Terengganu High Court today awarded RM47,000 in damages and costs to a boy, now 13, who suffered a broken right leg in an incident involving a Quran and Fardu Ain (KAFA) teacher four years ago. Judge Yusrin Faidz Yusoff allowed Muhammad Izz Anaqi Mohd Izwan’s appeal and set aside an earlier Sessions Court decision that had dismissed his claim, Utusan Malaysia reported. “The judge failed to assess the evidence of two eyewitnesses and the specialist medical report from Sultanah Nur Zahirah Hospital.

items.title: Anwar thanks outgoing China ambassador for strengthening ties with Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today expressed his appreciation to outgoing Chinese Ambassador to Malaysia, Ouyang Yujing, for his commitment and contribution towards strengthening cooperation between the two countries. Anwar conveyed his appreciation when he received a farewell call from Ouyang today. He said Malaysia and China had built strong ties across various sectors, including the economy, technology, education and culture.

items.title: Afghanistan says deadly Pakistani strikes hit Helmand
items.summary: KABUL: The Pakistani military launched rare deadly strikes on Afghanistan's Helmand province on Thursday, the Taliban government and residents told AFP. The latest strikes hit Helmand as well as Kunar, which borders Pakistan, killing 10 civilians, according to the Taliban government's deputy spokesman Hamdullah Fitrat. Two Helmand residents told AFP that three airstrikes hit their village.

items.title: Selangor employers who chose Sultan’s Silver Jubilee Oct 25 holiday must observe it, says Labour Dept
items.summary: The department said the special public holiday was declared under subsection 9(1) of the Holidays Act 1951 [Act 369], which allows the state government to declare any day as a public holiday in the state. On September 11, the Selangor state government announced October 26 as a replacement public holiday for the entire state following the declaration of October 25 as a special public holiday in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration. Selangor State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the replacement holiday was declared because the celebration and the special public holiday fell on a Sunday.

items.title: Nga Kor Ming offers one month’s ministerial salary for top Housing Ministry innovator
items.summary: He said there is ample scope for innovation at the Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) as it oversees housing, local government, cleanliness and solid waste management, fire and rescue services, as well as urban planning, all of which have a direct impact on people’s lives. He said this in his speech at the 2026 Ministry of Housing and Local Government Innovation Day (HIKPKT 2026) here today. HIKPKT 2026, themed “ Memperkasa Inovasi, Memacu Prestasi, Menyejahtera Rakyat ”, showcased 54 innovation projects, including 43 Innovative and Creative Group (KIK) projects and 11 Minister’s Innovation Award (AIM) projects.

items.title: Something next week? Amirudin signals movement in Pakatan-Bersatu talks for Melaka polls
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 1 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) could see a development in its talks with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia as early as next week, its election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today, as the coalition weighs its options ahead of the Melaka state election. Amirudin said PH remained in discussions with various parties and had not ruled out cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN), with all possibilities still on the table. The Selangor menteri besar said PH’s immediate priority in the negotiations was securing electoral success, but stressed that any arrangement would also have to serve the interests of the people.

items.title: RM35 nasi lemak, RM30 Indomie: F1 food prices rev up at Sepang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Formula 1 fans heading to Sepang this weekend might want to leave a little extra room in the budget, with a plate of nasi lemak and fried egg listed at RM35 on an official vendor menu for the race. Four chicken rice meals would come to RM120, while four portions of cut fruit would cost RM80. The prices are listed on a vendor menu circulated through the event’s official QR ordering link .

items.title: Selangor Sultan marks silver jubilee with joyride flight for 149 orphans
items.summary: SUBANG, Oct 1 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and Tengku Permaisuri Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin today treated 149 orphans to a special joyride flight to mark the Sultan’s 25th anniversary on the throne. Their Royal Highnesses, accompanied by Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah, were welcomed at Subang SkyPark by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. Istana Alam Shah, in a statement, said that the Kembara Semenanjung Joyride Flight, involving children from 29 orphanages, officially kicked off the month-long Selangor Sultan Silver Jubilee celebrations in October.

items.title: Malaysia, Singapore eye stronger business links to boost intra-Asean trade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Malaysia and Singapore can collaborate to enhance business connectivity within Asean and boost intra-Asean trade by leveraging their strengths in supply chains, the digital economy, and key industries. Miti Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said both countries could explore ways to facilitate greater trade and business linkages among Asean member states, with the long-term objective of increasing the share of intra-Asean trade. The total trade among the 11 countries in Asean is US$4.37 trillion, and among us Asean is only about US$800 billion to US$900 billion.

items.title: US$2m ‘scratch and win’ scam busted in Penang, 29 arrested
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Penang police have busted an international scam syndicate targeting victims, particularly in China and Cambodia, with the arrest of 29 foreign nationals in raids on three bungalows used as call centres in Barat Daya on September 22. The first raid in Teluk Kumbar led to the arrest of 14 Chinese men who had no travel documents, while the second raid in the same area resulted in the detention of three Chinese men, a Cambodian man and three Cambodian women. “The third raid at Solok Bukit Belah, Bayan Baru, saw two Chinese men and six Cambodian women arrested.

items.title: MRT Corp: Overnight lane closures on Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah in George Town until Nov 30 for Mutiara Line works
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 1 — Long-term, periodic partial road closures on Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah here will be implemented from today until November 30 to facilitate construction work for the Mutiara Line Light Rail Transit (LRT) project in the area. In a statement, Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp) announced that the closures affecting the stretch from Sungai Nibong Bus Terminal to Batu Uban Road Transport Department (RTD) office will take place between 10pm and 5am to allow for tree cutting and relocation works. “The closures will affect the leftmost lane between Lorong Sungai Dua 1 residential area and Batu Uban RTD office (towards Komtar), as well as the rightmost lane between Lorong Sungai Dua 1 residential area and Batu Uban RTD office in both directions.

items.title: MACC to take six anti-graft proposals before national governance committee
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Six resolutions adopted at the Fifth National Research Conference on Governance, Integrity and Anti-Corruption (TIAR) 2026 last Friday will be submitted for consideration by the Special Cabinet Committee on National Governance (JKKTN) at its next meeting. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said this was to ensure the resolutions were translated into concrete improvements to the system, particularly efforts to strengthen corruption prevention, rather than remaining merely conference outcomes. Abd Halim said submitting the resolutions to the JKKTN was in line with MACC’s approach of strengthening corruption prevention through a more proactive, targeted and risk-based strategy.

items.title: Penang man charged with secretly filming four women using factory toilet
items.summary: Berita Harian reported that Muhammad Mukhris Sulaiman pleaded not guilty to all five charges and claimed trial after they were read out before Magistrate Sharifah Razali at the Magistrate’s Court in Bukit Mertajam today. For the first four charges, Muhammad Mukhris is accused of filming the women at a factory in Bukit Minyak, in the Central Seberang Perai district, between 11.44am and 6.55pm from September 2 to September 23. Muhammad Mukhris was also charged with possessing several obscene videos during an inspection at the Seberang Perai Tengah district police headquarters compound at 9.30am on September 24.

items.title: Nearly two billion e-invoices submitted by 268,000 taxpayers as of Oct 1, says Inland Revenue Board
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — More than 268,000 taxpayers have submitted 1.99 billion e-invoices as of October 1, the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) said. Its chief executive officer Datuk Abu Tariq Jamaluddin said 196,031 taxpayers accounted for submissions under phase four of the e-invoicing rollout. Abu Tariq said 5,582 taxpayers had submitted e-invoices under phase one, followed by 14,579 under phase two and 51,815 under phase three.

items.title: Education Ministry halts school programmes involving freelance speakers amid allegations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek has ordered the immediate suspension of all programmes involving freelance speakers in schools following allegations circulating on social media involving a freelance speaker who had previously conducted programmes with pupils. Fadhlina said she was aware of several allegations involving the speaker and had instructed the Education Ministry to obtain further information on the matter. Her statement came after allegations involving the freelance speaker and school pupils circulated on social media.

items.title: ‘If the price is me, I’ll pay it’: Border agency chief Shuhaily ready to face action over viral KLIA incident
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said he was prepared to accept any action taken by the government over a viral video from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), saying he would take responsibility for what happened. Therefore, whatever decision they make, I will accept it,” he said, according to Utusan Malaysia . Shuhaily said two unidentified individuals then appeared and began filming while officers were interviewing the foreign national.

items.title: ICJ? Asean? Civil suits? What can Malaysia, others do about Indonesia’s choking haze?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 — Haze from Indonesian wildfires has blanketed neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore for more than a month, closing schools and sending respiratory complaints skyrocketing. It is not the first time Indonesian haze has caused a regional pollution crisis, but neighbouring countries have few options for legal recourse, experts say: Case at the ICJ Suggestions that Malaysia and Singapore take Indonesia to the UN’s highest judicial organ, the International Court of Justice in The Hague, face a basic obstacle: “The main issue is jurisdiction, as the ICJ generally requires the consent of both states,” said Professor Mohd Hazmi Mohd Rusli of Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia. Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore are neither signatories nor parties to the 1979 Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution, a European-centred treaty framework intended to curb cross-border air pollution.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan DAP lodges police report over Facebook post linking party to ongoing crisis, royal institution
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 1 — Negeri Sembilan DAP today lodged a police report over a social media post allegedly linking the party to the state’s ongoing crisis and royal institution. State DAP chairman J. Arul Kumar said a post by a Facebook account under the name Khalide Al Walid had, among other things, alleged links between the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and DAP, as well as connecting the party to issues involving customary land. He said the post also allegedly linked DAP to several other issues, including customary land, elected representatives attending religious briefings and the renaming of roads.

items.title: Kuala Pilah hostel death: Form Four student’s remand extended seven days until Oct 8
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Oct 1 — The remand order for a 16-year-old male student detained to assist investigations into the death of a Form Two student at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah on September 25 has been extended by seven days. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the suspect’s extended remand runs from October 2 to October 8, following an order issued by the Kuala Pilah Magistrates’ Court today, Sinar Harian reported. He said police have so far recorded statements from 70 individuals, including students, teachers and coaches.

items.title: Bukit Aman JPJKK chief Noor Hisam Nordin heads list of Pahang state awards recipients
items.summary: Al-Sultan Abdullah officiated the investiture ceremony at Balai Mahkota, Istana Abdulaziz, here today, with the Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah, and the Tengku Mahkota of Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah, also in attendance. Also present were Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and the state government leadership. Noor Hisam, who is also a former Deputy Chief of Pahang Police, received the Sri Sultan Ahmad Shah Pahang (SSAP), which carries the title of Datuk Seri.

items.title: Health Ministry urges 4,255 UD10 medical officers to report for duty by Oct 7
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 1 — The Health Ministry (MOH) has urged Medical Officers Grade UD10 who have yet to report for duty to do so immediately before the October 7 deadline. In a statement today carried by Bernama, MOH said the officers concerned must complete the reporting-in process at their respective Responsibility Centres (PTj). “The process of reporting for duty for Medical Officers Grade UD10 (Phase 2), who were appointed on a permanent basis effective September 28, 2026, is still ongoing and has yet to be completed.

items.title: Man remanded after 100km police chase in Pasir Gudang ends with lorry ramming patrol car
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 — A man accused of driving a stolen lorry against traffic and ramming a pursuing police car in Pasir Gudang has been remanded for three days to assist police investigations. Police said yesterday that the suspect was arrested after allegedly fleeing in a lorry stolen from Plentong. During the chase, the lorry allegedly rammed a police car after the driver refused to stop.
